content:
Looks pretty interesting. The latest ChatGPT update adds a new Mac integration: the ability to handle conversations within Apple's Messages app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now has an Apple Messages extension

The new Apple Messages extension lets ChatGPT read and search chat histories on your Mac, and compose and send messages. OpenAI says this feature is available across all plans for the ChatGPT macOS desktop app, and supports both ChatGPT and Codex.

Given the access involved, this naturally raises privacy and control issues. OpenAI emphasises that, by default, sending messages requires user approval. Users should think carefully before granting persistent approval. OpenAI's extension guidance details the related risks, how to revoke permissions, and a known issue involving bypassing the approval prompt.

At this stage the feature is only available on Macs with Apple Silicon; Intel models are not supported.

If you ask ChatGPT to send a message on your behalf, the system pops up a confirmation prompt before sending. You can also choose to skip this confirmation step on a per-conversation basis.

Want to find this new feature in ChatGPT? The link below will take you straight to the Messages extension for ChatGPT for Mac.

Collaborative site editing, conversation snapshot sharing, and more

Although the Messages extension is the headline new feature for Apple users, this release also includes a number of other improvements. For example, pinned conversations can now stay in sync between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, letting users access important conversations on their Mac and iPhone whenever they like.

ChatGPT now also lets users share read-only snapshots of local Codex conversations. These snapshots do not change when the original conversation is updated.

Links generated from a personal account can be opened by anyone with the URL; workspace links, however, can only be opened by members of that workspace. OpenAI says Codex masks known sensitive formats, but reminds users to check their own snapshots, since they may still contain sensitive data.

In addition, site owners can invite existing members of the same workspace to co-edit a site with collaboration enabled. Editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish updates once the owner has completed the initial publish. Owners retain control over access, settings, analytics, and version rollback.

Some site owners can also change the URL hosted by ChatGPT without redeploying, with the old address automatically redirecting to the new one.

Finally, the computer use history feature launched last week is now being expanded to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK. This opt-in feature requires the Memory feature to be enabled in order to work, and is off by default.

You can check out the full release notes for this update here.
